newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australia's NSW sets A$400 mln in new taxes.
newsitem.headline: Australia's NSW sets A$400 mln in new taxes.

text.p: The Australian state of New South Wales introduced new tax measures worth almost A$400 million in its 1997/98 budget released on Tuesday.

Treasurer Michael Egan told state parliament the taxes, including an electricity distributor's levy, an increase in land tax and a duty on central business district (CBD) accommodation, were designed as far as possible to protect the less well off.
The main new revenue measures and their projected raisings are listed below.
*Introduction of electricty distributors' levy -- A$100 million
*Land tax increase to 1.85 percent from 1.65 percent and extended coverage to high valued owner occupied properties -- A$109 million
*Increasing club gaming device duty -- A$56 million
*Increasing the concessional rate of duty on general insurance -- A$51 million
*Introduction of CBD accomodation duty -- A$48 million
*Increased stamp duty on luxury vehicles -- A$10 million
*Doubling of CBD parking space levy -- A$7.8 million
